internationalAid.note: Union states that international students can receive academic scholarships but no other university financial aid. It does not commit to meet international financial need, so applicants must plan for the remaining cost.

scholarships.note: International students may receive academic merit scholarships. internationalAdmission.note: International undergraduates submit Union's application, official academic result meeting one approved English or academic-test threshold, a course-by-course NACES evaluation in most cases, and the financial and immigration materials needed for Form I-20. Union does not publish a current international admit rate.

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: Union uses rolling admission beginning each September and continues until the class is full. applicationRequirements.note: Applicants submit Union's undergraduate application and $35 fee, an official test meeting an approved threshold, and a course-by-course NACES evaluation in most cases. The international forms also cover finances and the Statement of Understanding; official school records are required.

testingPolicy.note: Union has a limited test-optional route capped at 5% of the entering class and requires admitted test-optional students to join the Keystone Program. Submitted ACT, SAT or CLT results are superscored. International applicants whose first language is not English still meet an approved English or academic-test threshold.

englishProficiency.note: Accepted minimums are TOEFL 80, IELTS 6.5, iTEP 3.9, Duolingo 105, ACT 22, SAT 1020 on the older critical-reading-plus-math measure, or SAT 1100 on evidence-based reading and writing plus math.

facts.testingPolicy: Limited test-optional route capped at 5% of the entering class; Union superscores submitted results
facts.internationalAidPolicy: Academic scholarships only; no other university aid or full-need commitment for international students

internationalAid.note: UC Santa Cruz does not offer need-based financial assistance to international students. Applicants must document sufficient funds for nonresident tuition, university charges and living expenses after admission.

scholarships.note: New international first-year students are considered for the Undergraduate Dean's Award, currently listed at $12,000 to $100,000 total across four years. The UC admission application also serves as the scholarship application; international students should not expect need-based UC aid.

internationalAdmission.note: International first-year applicants complete the UC application, report all coursework exactly as it appears without converting grades, satisfy UC subject and secondary-completion requirements, and demonstrate English when applicable. They do not send transcripts or extra documents with the application. UCSC does not publish a current international admit rate.

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: For Fall 2027, the UC application filing deadline is November 30, 2026. UCSC does not offer ED, EA, REA or ED2 for first-year applicants; the single UC deadline and later UC notification and enrollment dates apply.

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants use the University of California application, self-report all international coursework and grades as shown on the original record, complete the UC personal-insight and activity sections, and satisfy subject, secondary-completion and English requirements. Do not send recommendations, transcripts, awards or extra materials unless requested after admission.

testingPolicy.note: UC campuses do not consider SAT or ACT for admission decisions or scholarships. Submitted scores may only support limited eligibility requirements or placement after enrollment, and English-proficiency evidence remains separate.

englishProficiency.note: Applicants with fewer than three years of English-medium secondary schooling generally need proof. Current routes include TOEFL new-scale 4.5, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 115, ACT English Language Arts 24, SAT Writing and Language 31, qualifying AP or IB English results, or an approved UC-transferable composition course.

facts.testingPolicy: UC does not consider SAT or ACT for admission or scholarships
facts.internationalAidPolicy: No international need-based aid; automatic consideration for the Undergraduate Dean's Award

internationalAid.note: UHV offers international merit and cultural scholarships but does not publish a commitment to meet full international need. Applicants submit sponsorship and recent bank evidence covering the remaining first-year cost.

scholarships.note: The International Student Cultural Scholarship provides $1,500 per year for up to nine undergraduate semesters, subject to full-time F-1 or J-1 enrollment, 2.5 GPA, timely bills, orientation and five volunteer hours each semester. UHV also has a separate competitive merit application whose current award amount is not published.

internationalAdmission.note: International freshmen use ApplyTexas, pay $25, submit official secondary credentials and English translations, English evidence, F-1 Student Agreement, sponsorship and bank documentation, and passport. UHV reviews international academic credentials internally and does not publish a current international admit rate.

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: UHV's current international page lists April 1 as the fall priority date and June 1 as the final fall date, plus separate spring and summer dates. The page does not label them specifically for Fall 2027, so they are planning references.

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants submit ApplyTexas and the $25 fee, official secondary transcripts and certificates with professional English translation, approved English evidence, F-1 Student Agreement, Letter of Financial Sponsorship with recent bank documents, and passport. SAT and ACT are optional.

testingPolicy.note: SAT and ACT are optional for international freshman admission. Applicants still submit official proof meeting UHV's English-proficiency requirement unless an official exemption applies.

englishProficiency.note: UHV's current freshman page requires official Duolingo, TOEFL, IELTS, TIEC or other approved English evidence but does not publish the minimum scores on that page, and the linked detailed requirement page was not available during review. Applicants should confirm current minimums before ordering scores.

facts.testingPolicy: SAT and ACT optional; official English evidence required unless exempt
facts.internationalAidPolicy: $1,500 annual cultural scholarship plus competitive international merit; no full-need commitment

internationalAid.note: UMF's current public materials require international students to document enough financial support for at least one academic year, but they do not publish a current international need-aid policy or commitment to meet full need.

scholarships.note: UMF publishes current merit awards for Maine residents, not a current international scholarship grid. Its finance form recognizes that a student may hold a UMF scholarship, but no Fall 2027 international amount, eligibility rule, application route, or renewal requirement is published.

internationalAdmission.note: The latest detailed official international admission instructions available in the public UMF catalog require official secondary and college records with certified translations, English evidence, and full first-year financial documentation. UMF has not published a current Fall 2027 international checklist or international admit rate.

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: An older official UMF catalog lists March 1 for international fall materials, while still older catalogs list June 1. Because the official sources conflict and no Fall 2027 date is published, neither date should be treated as current; applicants must confirm directly with UMF.

applicationRequirements.note: The older official checklist uses Common Application or University of Maine System Application and requires official school records with certified translations, English evidence, and documentation covering the full first-year cost for Form I-20. Current Fall 2027 document and fee rules are not published.

testingPolicy.note: A legacy University of Maine System application describes UMF as SAT/ACT optional, but UMF has not published a current Fall 2027 standardized-testing policy on its public admission pages. Applicants should verify before withholding scores.

englishProficiency.note: An older official catalog lists TOEFL 79 or IELTS 6.0 and a possible waiver after at least two years of English-medium instruction. These are prior-cycle planning references, not confirmed Fall 2027 minimums.

facts.testingPolicy: Fall 2027 SAT and ACT policy not published; an older system application was test-optional
facts.internationalAidPolicy: Current international aid and scholarship terms not published; first-year funding evidence is required

internationalAid.note: UMD offers a renewable International Student Scholarship but does not publish a commitment to meet full international need. Applicants must plan for the remaining tuition and living costs.

scholarships.note: The International Student Scholarship awards up to $5,000 annually, or $20,000 across four years, and renews with full-time undergraduate enrollment and a 3.0 University of Minnesota GPA. A completed fall application by May 1 is required for consideration.

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants complete UMD's online application, pay $50, submit high-school records and English evidence, and receive an individual review in the context of their national education system. UMD does not publish a current international admit rate.

applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: UMD lists May 1 as the international fall priority date and June 15 as the final date, with November 15 and December 1 for spring. The page does not identify these dates specifically for Fall 2027, so they are planning references.

applicationRequirements.note: Applicants submit UMD's online application and $50 nonrefundable fee, secondary-school records, and approved English evidence unless exempt. Unofficial records can support review, but official final records are required; international application fee waivers are not offered.

testingPolicy.note: UMD is test-optional for SAT and ACT, including international applicants. English proficiency verification is still required for most international students, and submitted academic scores may support advising and placement.

englishProficiency.note: Minimums are TOEFL iBT 71, IELTS 6.0, Duolingo 105, Cambridge 175, PTE 54, ACT English and Reading 21, or SAT Reading and Writing 540. Country, AP/A-Level/IB English, U.S. coursework and U.S. high-school routes can provide exemptions.

facts.testingPolicy: SAT and ACT optional for international applicants; English proficiency remains required unless exempt
facts.internationalAidPolicy: Renewable International Student Scholarship up to $5,000 annually; no full-need commitment

scholarships.note: The international page confirms scholarship eligibility, and general first-year scholarship consideration uses a February 1 admission target, but Montevallo does not publish a current international-specific award grid, guaranteed amount, or Fall 2027 scholarship deadline.

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants submit the university application, passport, fee, official academic records and NACES evaluation, approved English evidence, medical materials, and a financial affidavit with bank documentation. applicationRequirements.note: Applicants submit Montevallo's application and $30 fee, passport, translated official academic records with a NACES evaluation, approved English evidence, financial affidavit with bank proof, and required international medical documents.

testingPolicy.note: SAT and ACT are optional for general undergraduate admission. International applicants still meet English proficiency, while individual scholarships or programs may request scores.

englishProficiency.note: Minimums are TOEFL iBT 71, IELTS overall 6.0 with no section below 5.0, PTE 48, or Duolingo 105.

facts.internationalAidPolicy: No international financial-aid program; scholarship eligibility exists without a published current award grid

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants apply free, submit secondary and any college transcripts, meet a 2.8 U.S.-equivalent GPA expectation, demonstrate English, and complete the application addendum and proof of funding after initial review. applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: USF's current international page does not publish Fall 2027 ED, EA, RD, priority, rolling, document, or notification dates. Applicants should confirm the latest date for admission and Form I-20 processing.

applicationRequirements.note: There is no application fee. testingPolicy.note: The international checklist accepts ACT or SAT section results as English evidence but does not publish a separate Fall 2027 SAT/ACT admission policy. Applicants can meet English through TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, English-medium study or U.S. coursework.

facts.testingPolicy: Fall 2027 general SAT/ACT policy not published; ACT or SAT may satisfy an English route
facts.internationalAidPolicy: Current international aid and scholarship eligibility not fully published; proof of funding is required

scholarships.note: International applicants remain eligible for university merit scholarships when applying test-optional, while some competitive awards can require scores. The current official pages do not publish a complete Fall 2027 international merit range or guaranteed award amount.

internationalAdmission.note: International freshmen apply online, provide a professional credential evaluation for secondary work outside the United States, and demonstrate English for direct or conditional admission. applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: An official international guide recommends June 15 for August entry and October 15 for January entry, but the guide is not labeled for Fall 2027. The current web checklist publishes no ED, EA, RD, priority, document, or notification schedule.

applicationRequirements.note: The online application has no fee. Applicants submit an application, professional credential evaluation for school work outside the United States, and English evidence. testingPolicy.note: Domestic and international first-year students may apply test-optional to any degree program, and SAT or ACT is not required for university merit consideration. International freshmen must still demonstrate English; some competitive scholarships may require scores.

englishProficiency.note: Direct-admission routes include TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.0, SAT 1030, ACT 20, plus other published exams and accredited English-program completion. facts.internationalAidPolicy: Academic scholarships available; no published international full-need commitment or current award grid

internationalAdmission.note: International applicants submit the application, official secondary records and certified translations, a credential evaluation where required, approved English evidence, and supporting financial and immigration documents. applicationPlansAndDeadlines.note: The current international admission page does not publish Fall 2027 ED, EA, RD, priority, final, document, or notification dates. Older official catalogs list July 1, but that date is too old to use as a current planning reference.

facts.internationalAidPolicy: International institutional need application available; no published full-need commitment or current merit grid

scholarships.note: Valparaiso reports substantial undergraduate scholarship support and participates in international award programs, but its current official pages available during review do not publish a complete Fall 2027 international merit range, automatic consideration rule, or renewal terms.

internationalAdmission.note: The accessible official international procedure covers exchange applicants and requires an application, university transcript, passport, financial documentation and English evidence. testingPolicy.note: Valparaiso has not published an accessible official Fall 2027 SAT/ACT policy on the reviewed undergraduate pages. No assumption is made from older or third-party sources.
